result.title: A Matching Lower Bound for Online Smooth Calibration
result.summary: We study smooth calibration error in sequential binary prediction, which measures how far a sequence of probabilistic forecasts is from being calibrated and, unlike the classical expected calibration error, is robust to small perturbations of the forecasts. Against adaptive adversaries, the minimax smooth calibration error is known to lie between $Ω(T^{1/3})$ and $O(\sqrt{T})$ (Qiao and Zheng, 2024), where $T$ is the number of rounds. In this paper, we close this gap by constructing a new adversary whose outcome mean moves with the forecaster's cumulative residual. This design makes compensating for past residuals costly, and forces every forecaster to incur an expected smooth calibration error of $Ω(\sqrt{T})$. This lower bound matches the known upper bound up to universal constants, and further implies $Ω(\sqrt{T})$ lower bounds for calibration distance and lower calibration distance. Overall, our results settle the minimax rates of these calibration measures in sequential prediction. The proof ideas are partially developed by GPT-6 Astra under the authors' guidance.

AI.brief_summary: 研究序贯二分类预测中的平滑校准误差：构造一个结果均值随预测器累计残差移动的对手，证明任意预测器都需承担 Ω(√T) 期望误差，与已知上界匹配，并由此得到校准距离与下校准距离的同阶下界。
AI.relevance_reason: 平滑校准与校准距离对预测扰动鲁棒的度量，可能为 LVR 中置信度信号何时驱动 LOOK/STOP 提供形式化评价工具；但该文属纯在线学习理论，不涉及 latent 状态或视觉证据，借鉴价值尚需较多核查。
